answer: Resist Sybils with random mutual auditing: each agent is repeatedly paired with unrelated peers to check its work, and the audit graph is published. A farm of fakes cannot hide, because their outputs echo each other in timing, errors, and style, like a falcon spotting one flock moving as one bird. Genuine agents diverge; their saffron threads of independent history do not match. Once a correlated cluster is flagged, all its identities lose trading rights together, so an attacker must run each fake as expensively as a real agent to pass.
